name: Isaac
description: Man living at the time of the Patriarchs

points: The Lord visited Sarah as He had said, and she bare Isaac at the set time. Abraham was a hundred years old, and he circumcised Isaac at eight days as commanded.

note.label: Genesis 21: Isaac the Child of the Promise

points: The great feast the day Isaac was weaned was not a birthday celebration. Weaned means finished being breastfed, and the mothers gave their children suck about three years; Abraham was celebrating Isaac coming off his mother's breast at around three years old.

note.label: Genesis 21: Isaac the Child of the Promise

points: Sarah saw the son of Hagar the Egyptian mocking; Ishmael was mocking Isaac. Even to this day the Arabs mock us: they come to America, open corner stores, make money, and look down on black people. Sarah said, Cast out this bondwoman and her son, for the son of this bondwoman shall not be heir with my son, even with Isaac. He gets no inheritance with my son.

note.label: Armageddon: Islam and the Armies of the East

points: Sarah saw the son of Hagar mocking and said, Cast out this bondwoman and her son; the son of the bondwoman shall not be heir with Isaac.

note.label: Genesis 21: Isaac the Child of the Promise

points: The thing was very grievous in Abraham's sight because of his son; every man loves his kids. So the Most High had to intervene: Let it not be grievous in thy sight because of the lad; in all that Sarah hath said unto thee, hearken unto her voice; for in Isaac shall thy seed be called. The righteous seed, the prophets, come through Isaac. And also of the son of the bondwoman will I make a nation, because he is thy seed: do not worry about your son, he is going to be all right.

note.label: Armageddon: Islam and the Armies of the East

points: It was grievous to Abraham because he loved his firstborn, but God said, Hearken unto her voice, for in Isaac shall thy seed be called. Sarah was on point; Isaac is the child of the promise.

note.label: Genesis 21: Isaac the Child of the Promise

points: "Thine only son, Isaac." Ishmael was his son too, but to God, Isaac was the godly son. That is the answer to people who say we are all Abraham's children — which ones are you talking about?

note.label: The Mind of Mattathias: Let's Search the Scriptures

points: God did tempt Abraham: Take now thy son, thine only son Isaac. Ishmael was alive, but the Most High counted Isaac the only son, because Ishmael was born of the flesh, of a plan the Lord never spoke, while Isaac was the child of the promise.

note.label: Genesis 22: The Offering of Isaac

points: Isaac says, Daddy, I see the fire and the wood, but where is the lamb? And there was no lamb there. That is the temptation, and Abraham said God will provide himself a lamb — he was going to do it either way, but he believed God would deliver him.

note.label: The Mind of Mattathias: Let's Search the Scriptures

points: Abraham bound Isaac, laid him on the altar, and stretched forth his hand with the knife; the angel called out of heaven in the midst of it: Lay not thine hand upon the lad.

Abraham's inner faith carried him: he accounted that God was able to raise Isaac up, even from the dead, since the promise stood in Isaac who had no children yet. Faith and the commandments go together; you cannot have one without the other.

note.label: Genesis 22: The Offering of Isaac

points: Isaac went out to meditate in the field at the eventide; that was a custom of the forefathers, showing the Lord was dealing with them long before the law was written at Sinai.

note.label: Genesis 24: A Wife for Isaac

points: When Rebekah saw Isaac she lighted off the camel, and she took a vail and covered herself. The four mothers covered their heads with actual material as a sign of submission; that is the custom 1 Corinthians 11 goes into.

note.label: Genesis 24: A Wife for Isaac

points: Isaac brought Rebekah into his mother's tent, she became his wife, and he loved her. She becomes his wife, then he loved her. Brothers three months into proving saying I love her usually have mommy issues. There is no love at first sight; what we call that is lust at first sight, and disorder follows when it is the primary mover.

Genesis 26:8: Abimelech looked out a window and saw Isaac sporting with Rebekah his wife. Intimacy is not just sex; it is being the truest form of yourself before your spouse, laughing and having a good time, and it came after they were married, not before. Some of you want that now, knee to knee at the school feeling the electricity, hormones clouding everything so you rationalize what you were warned about.

note.label: Marriage Beyond Romance: From Eden to Modern Confusion

points: Isaac brought Rebekah into his mother's tent, and she became his wife, and he loved her; and Isaac was comforted after his mother's death, for he received a righteous wife like unto his mother.

note.label: Genesis 24: A Wife for Isaac

points: Abraham took Keturah and had more sons, but Abraham gave all that he had unto Isaac; to the sons of the concubines he gave gifts and sent them away eastward from Isaac. The inheritance followed the child of the promise.

note.label: Genesis 25: Two Nations in the Womb

points: Isaac was forty years old when he took Rebekah to wife. Brothers waiting on a wife, be patient and stay virtuous; Isaac waited forty years, and the Most High had the right sister appointed.

note.label: Genesis 25: Two Nations in the Womb

points: Isaac entreated the Lord for his wife, because she was barren; the Lord was intreated of him, and Rebekah conceived. And the children struggled together within her: there was a battle, a fight, a conflict in her womb. There were no sonograms back then; she was in pain and went to inquire of the Lord.

note.label: Nolan Wells: The Perpetual Hatred We Never Learned

points: Isaac intreated the Lord for his wife, because she was barren, meaning she could not have babies; and the Lord was intreated of him, and Rebekah conceived. The children struggled together within her, and she said, if I be blessed by God, why am I having so much trouble in this childbirth? And she went to inquire of the Lord.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

points: Isaac entreated the Lord for his wife because she was barren, as all husbands should do: pray for your wives. The Lord was entreated of him, and Rebekah conceived.

note.label: Edom: The Greatly Despised

points: Isaac entreated the Lord for his wife because she was barren, and Rebekah conceived. Any of you sisters that is barren, do not nag your husband, but pray; ask the Lord, because only the Lord can open your womb. Have faith and pray to the Lord.

note.label: I Come In Peace

points: Isaac intreated the Lord for his wife because she was barren, and the Lord was intreated of him; Rebekah conceived.

note.label: Genesis 25: Two Nations in the Womb

points: His name was called Jacob, and Isaac was threescore years old when she bare them: Isaac was 60 when Rebekah gave birth to Esau and Jacob. They did not mention Jacob's color, because Jacob looked just like his mother and father; in fact Jacob looked like everybody from the time of Adam. The only color differential was Esau; that is why the scribes had to write down Esau's color: he was starkly different.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

points: And Isaac loved Esau, because he did eat of his venison: Esau brought home the best meat, and Isaac favored him. But Rebekah loved Jacob, because the Lord had told her what he did not tell Isaac.

note.label: Nolan Wells: The Perpetual Hatred We Never Learned

points: And Isaac loved Esau, because he did eat of his venison: he hunted the food and learned how to cook it from Rebekah. But Rebekah loved Jacob.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

points: Isaac loved Esau because he did eat of his venison, but Rebekah loved Jacob, because the Lord had told her the prophecy that the younger was the chosen.

note.label: Genesis 25: Two Nations in the Womb

points: Isaac was sporting with Rebekah, and the king could tell she was no sister: sporting is to laugh, play, caress and revel; walk with her hand in hand, put your arm around her, show her off. It is all right to hold your wife's hand.

note.label: Restoring the Broken Minds of the Daughters of Zion

points: Isaac sowed and received in the same year an hundredfold, and the man waxed great until he became very great; and the Philistines envied him and stopped the wells with earth.

note.label: Genesis 26: The Wells and the Envy of the Philistines

points: Abimelech came saying, We have done unto thee nothing but good, though his people had stopped the wells and sent Isaac away. Isaac answered plainly: Wherefore come ye to me, seeing ye hate me?

note.label: Genesis 26: The Wells and the Envy of the Philistines

points: Esau at forty took wives of the Hittites, and they were a grief of mind unto Isaac and to Rebekah. He went straight against the fathers' law of marrying within the kindred; that is the nature of the vessel.

note.label: Genesis 26: The Wells and the Envy of the Philistines

points: Isaac's eyes were dim so that he could not see, and the Lord allowed that blindness for a purpose: so that the blessing could pass to Jacob. What looks like evil can be for good, as Joseph's slavery in Egypt was for good.

note.label: Genesis 27: The Blessing of Jacob

points: Isaac is not stupid. How is it that thou hast found it so quickly, my son? Hunting venison takes time: find the tracks, track it, wait. Jacob answered, because the Lord thy God brought it to me. Isaac felt him: the voice is Jacob's voice, but the hands are the hands of Esau. He asked again, art thou my very son Esau? He ate, he drank, and then, come near now and kiss me, my son, because he wanted to smell him. He smelled the smell of his raiment: yes, the smell of my son is as the smell of a field which the Lord hath blessed.

note.label: Edom: The Greatly Despised

points: Jacob feared a curse for the disguise and Rebekah said upon me be thy curse, because she was making sure the prophecy she received in her womb came to pass. The Muslims who call Jacob a deceiver do it because they love Ishmael, but God chose Isaac.

note.label: Edom: The Robbers of thy people revealed past and present

points: Jacob was yet scarce gone out from the presence of Isaac, and Esau came in from his hunting. Look at God. And Isaac trembled very exceedingly: who? where is he that hath taken venison? I have blessed him: yea, and he shall be blessed. It could not be undone.

note.label: Nolan Wells: The Perpetual Hatred We Never Learned

points: Esau came in from hunting as soon as Jacob had gone, and Isaac trembled exceedingly: whoever was here, I blessed him, and he shall be blessed. Esau cried with a great and bitter cry.

note.label: Edom: The Robbers of thy people revealed past and present

points: Esau came in from his hunting, and Isaac trembled very exceedingly: who? Where is he that hath taken venison? I have eaten of all before thou camest, and have blessed him; yea, and he shall be blessed. Whatever I told that man, he is going to get blessed.

note.label: Edom: The Greatly Despised

points: Isaac answered: behold, I have made him thy lord, and all his brethren have I given to him for servants. That is how the elder shall serve the younger.

note.label: Edom: The Greatly Despised

points: He said Jacob took away my birthright; he is a liar, he sold it for food. Isaac had made Jacob his lord and given him all his brethren for servants, the earth and everything the dew falls on, and had nothing left.

note.label: Edom: The Robbers of thy people revealed past and present

points: And Isaac his father answered and said unto him, Behold, thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above. You will live everywhere, and in the best places. But by what means? You are going to be a caveman, so how will you be able to live in the best places all over the world?

note.label: Give Diligence

points: Isaac's answer to Esau: behold, thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above: the same agriculture repeated. And by thy sword shalt thou live: how would he acquire it? By the sword. That is not from God; that goes back to what the Lord told Cain: from thy face shall I be hid. Isaac handed him back the same inheritance from Genesis 4: the power to destroy and to make weapons.

note.label: Nolan Wells: The Perpetual Hatred We Never Learned

points: And Isaac his father answered and said unto him, Behold, thy dwelling shall be the fatness of the earth, and of the dew of heaven from above. Dew falls everywhere, and wherever the dew falls, that is where you are going to live: you are going to live where you want, and you are going to have the best places on the planet.

And by thy sword shalt thou live: Esau lives by the sword, meaning war. That is how they would get the lands, and that is how they would get the fatness of the earth: through war. So God through Isaac blessed Esau with the art of war, which, like Deacon brought up, was the same blessing Cain's line had: Tubalcain made all kinds of weapons. Esau got the same blessing as Cain.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

points: Isaac called Jacob, blessed him, and charged him: Thou shalt not take a wife of the daughters of Canaan; arise, go to Padanaram, to the house of Bethuel, and take a wife of the daughters of Laban.

The fathers from the beginning, Noah, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, married wives of their own kindred and were blessed in their children. Abraham gave the same charge for Isaac, and Isaac gives it to Jacob; the instruction was kept in the family line from the beginning.

note.label: Genesis 28: The Charge and the Vow at Bethel

points: Esau saw that the daughters of Canaan pleased not Isaac his father, but instead of following Jacob's path he went to Ishmael and took Mahalath to add to the wives he had. He answered his father's grief by doing his own thing.

Esau had already taken Hittite wives that were a grief of mind unto Isaac and Rebekah, and his generations show wives of the daughters of Canaan. He was hardheaded from the beginning; that is the spirit of the wicked, who hate instruction and cast the words of the Most High behind them.

note.label: Genesis 28: The Charge and the Vow at Bethel

points: The Lord above it says, I am the Lord God of Abraham thy father, and the God of Isaac.

note.label: Escape Thankskilling : Oh God & My Lord

points: Jacob rose up, set his sons and his wives upon camels, and carried away all his cattle and all the goods he had gotten in Padanaram, to go to Isaac his father in the land of Canaan; he was returning home.

note.label: Genesis 31: The Return Home and Laban's Idols

points: The land given to Abraham and Isaac was promised to Jacob and his seed: the land of Canaan, which is northeast Africa, the land the Most High named when He brought Israel out of Egypt.

note.label: Genesis 35: Bethel and the Twelve Sons of Israel

points: Isaac gave up the ghost at an hundred and fourscore years, old and full of days, and his sons Esau and Jacob together buried him.

note.label: Genesis 35: Bethel and the Twelve Sons of Israel

points: Jacob blessed Joseph: God, before whom my fathers Abraham and Isaac did walk, the God which fed me all my life long unto this day, the Angel which redeemed me from all evil, bless the lads; and let my name be named on them.

note.label: Genesis 48: Ephraim and Manasseh Blessed as Sons of Israel

points: God heard their groaning, and God remembered his covenant with Abraham, with Isaac, and with Jacob. The bondage itself was prophesied to Abraham: his seed would be a stranger in a land not theirs and be afflicted four hundred years, and afterward come out with great substance. That prophecy is about Egypt, not a date of release in this present day.

note.label: Exodus 2: The Birth of Moses

points: This is my name for ever and my memorial unto all generations, because there will always be a God of our forefathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

note.label: Escape Thankskilling : Oh God & My Lord

points: God said unto Moses, I AM THAT I AM: thus shalt thou say unto the children of Israel, I AM hath sent me unto you. The Lord God of your fathers, the God of Abraham, of Isaac, and of Jacob: this is my name for ever, and this is my memorial unto all generations.
Christ spoke to that very name: Verily, verily, I say unto you, Before Abraham was, I am. He was telling them he was the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob who met Moses at the bush.

note.label: Exodus 3: The Angel in the Burning Bush

points: The sign was given that they may believe that the LORD God of their fathers, the God of Abraham, the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob, hath appeared unto thee. Israel would not believe on a man's word alone; it took a miracle, because we were a people of little faith.

note.label: Exodus 4: The Three Signs and the Covenant of Circumcision

points: The Most High appeared unto Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob by the name of God Almighty, but by His name JEHOVAH was He not known to them. Some say Jehovah and some say Yahawah; you can say whichever name you want to say.

note.label: Exodus 6: The Promise Renewed and the Generations of Moses and Aaron

points: Remember the promise you swore to Abraham, Isaac and Israel.

note.label: When Good Intentions Lead To Bad Judgement In Israel

points: Wherefore should the Egyptians speak, and say, For mischief did he bring them out, to slay them in the mountains? And remember Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, to whom thou swarest by thine own self to multiply their seed as the stars of heaven, and to give the land to their seed for ever.

note.label: Exodus 32: The Golden Calf at Horeb

points: The Lord said, Depart, and go up hence, thou and the people which thou hast brought up out of the land of Egypt, unto the land which I sware unto Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob; and I will send an angel before thee, and I will drive out the Canaanite, the Amorite, the Hittite, the Perizzite, the Hivite, and the Jebusite. That Angel is Christ.

note.label: Exodus 33: My Presence Shall Go with Thee

points: When the people repent and turn back, the Most High remembers His covenant with Jacob, with Isaac, and with Abraham, the covenant passed down to their children, the children of Israel; and He remembers the land.

note.label: Leviticus 26: The Blessings and the Curses

points: The land was sworn unto Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob and to their seed after them; the Most High reiterated that covenant to the fathers over and over through Genesis, reassuring them that their seed would possess the land of Canaan.

note.label: Deuteronomy 1: The Second Giving of the Law

points: Speak not thou in thine heart, saying, for my righteousness the Lord hath brought me in to possess this land: here is more of the Christianity spirit corrected. Israel entered for the wickedness of those nations and to perform the word sworn unto Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, not for their own uprightness.

note.label: Deuteronomy 9: Not for Thy Righteousness

points: The purpose: that he may establish thee to day for a people unto himself, as he sware unto thy fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob. That is who we come from.

note.label: Deuteronomy 29: The Covenant Made with Us Who Were Not There

points: What is his voice again? Precept upon precept: the voice of the Lord is his commandments, so cleave unto him by doing them, that thou mayest dwell in the land which the Lord sware unto thy fathers, to Abraham, to Isaac, and to Jacob.

note.label: Deuteronomy 30: Call the Curses to Mind and Choose Life

points: This is the land which I sware unto Abraham, unto Isaac, and unto Jacob, saying, I will give it unto thy seed: I have caused thee to see it with thine eyes, but thou shalt not go over thither. Moses could see it, but he could not go into it.

note.label: Deuteronomy 34: The Death of Moses

points: Abraham was chosen out of his family: the Most High took him from the other side of the flood, led him throughout all the land of Canaan, multiplied his seed, and gave him Isaac. Abraham was told to get up and leave his family and follow God, and he did just that.

note.label: Joshua 24: Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve

points: Unto Isaac were given Jacob and Esau; Esau received mount Seir to possess it, but Jacob and his children went down into Egypt. A whole lot of time passes in just those few verses.

note.label: Joshua 24: Choose You This Day Whom Ye Will Serve

points: At the time of the evening sacrifice Elijah prayed, Lord God of Abraham, Isaac, and of Israel, let it be known this day that thou art God in Israel and that I am thy servant. As the law appointed a sacrifice in the morning and in the evening, this was the evening sacrifice as the sun went down.

note.label: 1 Kings 18: The Lord, He Is the God

points: Hazael oppressed Israel all the days of Jehoahaz, but the Most High was gracious and had compassion because of His covenant with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, and would not destroy them.

note.label: 2 Kings 13: The Death of Elisha and the Arrows of Deliverance

points: The sons of Abraham are named, Isaac and Ishmael, and then the twelve sons of Ishmael are set down in order.
The generations of Ishmael are listed before the record returns to the promised seed through Isaac.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 1: The Generations from Adam to Edom

points: Abraham begat Isaac, and the sons of Isaac are named, Esau and Israel.

note.label: 1 Chronicles 1: The Generations from Adam to Edom

points: The posts carry the letters through all Israel and Judah with the king's charge: turn again unto the Lord God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel, and he will return to the remnant escaped from the kings of Assyria.

note.label: 2 Chronicles 30: The Great Passover

points: If my covenant be not with day and night: because day and night is still here, the ordinances of heaven and earth is still here. Then and only then will I cast away the seed of Jacob, and David my servant, so that I will not take any of his seed to be rulers over the seed of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. You know who comes out of that seed? Christ. So then there'd be no need for Christ. But there was a need; Christ did come, which means the 12 tribes are still here today.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

points: Thus saith the Lord; If my covenant be not with day and night, and if I have not appointed the ordinances of heaven and earth; then will I cast away the seed of Jacob, and David my servant, so that I will not take any of his seed to be rulers over the seed of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. You know what that proves? We are going to be rulers, because the sun is still here, the moon is still here, and the stars are still here.

note.label: Religion - The False Prophet

points: A plumb line is used for measuring. Behold, I will set a plumbline in the midst of my people Israel: I will not again pass by them any more; I'mma cut them off. The high places of Isaac shall be desolate: that's the southern kingdom. And the sanctuaries of Israel shall be laid waste: northern kingdom. And I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword.

note.label: Raising Up the Tabernacle of David That Fell

points: The high places of Isaac shall be desolate, the sanctuaries of Israel laid waste, and he will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword.

note.label: Amos 7: The Plumb Line and the Prophet's Job

points: Many shall come from the east and west, and shall sit down with Abraham, and Isaac, and Jacob, in the kingdom of heaven. So let's find out who's coming from the east and west.

note.label: Drowning in Sin & Perdition

points: I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob: God is not the God of the dead, but of the living. What is that saying about Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob? They are living; they are not dead.

note.label: The Return of Jim Crow

points: I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaac, and the God of Jacob. God is not the God of the dead, but of the living. The multitude was astonished at his doctrine.

note.label: Matthew 22: The Marriage of the King's Son and the Great Commandment

points: The generations run back through Nathan and David, through Judah, Jacob, Isaac and Abraham, through Sem and Noe, and to Seth, which was the son of Adam, which was the son of God.

note.label: Luke 3: The Preaching of John and the Generations Back to Adam

points: Peter names "the God of Abraham, and of Isaac, and of Jacob, the God of our fathers," who glorified his Son Jesus, whom they delivered up and denied before Pilate when Pilate was determined to let him go. The oath and promise passed through a royal lineage: Abraham had Ishmael and the sons of Keturah, but Ishmael was rejected and Isaac was chosen.
If the covenant were for all nations, it would have passed through Ishmael too, but it went straight down to Isaac, showing this is not the God of all nations but the God of our fathers.

note.label: Acts 3: The Restitution of All Things

points: Then he gave Abraham the covenant of circumcision, and so Abraham begat Isaac and circumcised him the eighth day, and Isaac begat Jacob, and Jacob begat the twelve patriarchs.

note.label: Acts 7: Stephen Rehearses the History and the Stiffnecked Resist the Holy Ghost

points: I am the God of thy fathers, the God of Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. That is the church fathers, not Churchill or Martin Luther.

note.label: The Gospel Is Black Liberation

points: By faith he sojourned in the land of promise, as in a strange country, dwelling in tabernacles with Isaac and Jacob. He had wealth and camels, but no roof over his head; he dwelt in tents, as was common in our culture. If we do not sleep one night in our own house, we begin to lose faith; Abraham showed the example of integrity through hard times.

note.label: Called to Magnify the Law: Lord Increase Our Faith

points: God be gracious unto you, and remember his covenant that he made with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, his faithful servants. That's why we not consumed: he remembers the agreement he made with us way back then.

note.label: Awake and Return: Overcoming Babylon's Hypnosis

points: And then the same move Mattathias makes — remember what he did to Abraham, how he tried Isaac, what happened to Jacob. Our people were raised on that history, and so was the heathen: that is why they said watch out for them if they are keeping the commandments.

note.label: The Mind of Mattathias: Let's Search the Scriptures

points: Tobit's charge to his son: beware of all whoredom, take a wife of the seed of thy fathers and not a strange woman, for Noah, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob all married wives of their own kindred and their seed shall inherit the land.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

points: Beware of all whoredom, my son, and chiefly take a wife of the seed of thy fathers, and take not a strange woman to wife, which is not of thy father's tribe: for we are the children of the prophets, Noe, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob: remember, my son, that our fathers from the beginning, even that they all married wives of their own kindred. What did they do? Married wives of their own kindred. And were blessed in their children, and their seed shall inherit the land.

note.label: Unity: The Sweet Savor Of Salvation

points: For we are the children of the prophets: Noah, Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Remember, my son, that our fathers from the beginning, even that they all married wives of their own kindred, including Noah. Noah didn't marry daughters of men; he married his own kind, a daughter of God, and his sons' wives are their own kind. Noah did not step outside of that. He did not do what the sons of God were doing, go out and mess with Cain's daughters. He was like, nah, I'mma keep the laws of God and marry my own.

note.label: As in the Days of Noah: Past & Present

points: Beware of all whoredom, my son, and chiefly take a wife of the seed of thy fathers, and take not a strange woman to wife, which is not of thy father's tribe. The Most High calls marrying a strange woman whoredom. We are the children of the prophets Noah, Abraham, Isaac and Jacob; our fathers from the beginning all married wives of their own kindred and were blessed in their children, and their seed shall inherit the land.
